name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Nebo who had married a foreign wife. Scripture highlights this particular detail about Jeiel, though it does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal notes. His mention occurs in the context of Ezra 10:43, emphasizing his family background and marriage choices.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel is a proper Hebrew name meaning 'G-d has preserved' or possibly 'G-d sweeps up.' This theophoric name reflects a connection to the divine name El, underscoring God's protective or cleansing role, although the name was not given directly by God according to the record in Ezra 10:43.
familyAndRelationships: Jeiel is explicitly described as a descendant of Nebo, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for Jeiel apart from his marriage to a foreign wife as noted in Ezra 10:43.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his representation within the post-exilic community, particularly in the context of the reforms recorded in Ezra. His marriage to a foreign wife is noted among those who were called to separate themselves from such unions, reflecting the community's commitment to covenant faithfulness and purity. This highlights the challenges faced by returning exiles in maintaining their identity and obedience to God's covenant.
